newsitem.title: USA: US Plains fed cattle rally may be poised to stall.
newsitem.headline: US Plains fed cattle rally may be poised to stall.

text.p: Trade in Plains feedlot cattle was slow Thursday amid concern the recent advance in prices may be losing momentum with packers apparently having plenty of inventory, feedlot sources said.
"Packers are bidding $65 and telling us they have comfortable inventory and if they do buy anything they would need 10 days to two weeks to pick up," one Kansas source said.

Cattle traded actively this week at $66 per cwt, up $2 from a week earlier. "I would like to think we were solid here and had the potential to go higher but it looks like we may be running out of gas," the Kansas source said.

Dealers in Texas and Kansas said the key of the market's trend was whether beef could move at the highest prices since December. USDA boxed beef values were higher again Thursday, showing gains of $0.02 to $0.24 per cwt.
"I would bet money the beef would start giving up some of that fairly quick or else start piling up on us," one feedlot source said.
The main unknown which could determine whether the beef can be moved appeared to be the export sector, amid some talk about a possible pick-up in demand from Japan.
